title: Building Reasoning LLMs for Hardware Design Generation via Function-Aligned Differentiated Revision
problem: LLM-based hardware generation produces functional errors and structural flaws. Current approaches focus on direct generation, yielding 27-44% pass rates. Lack reasoning capability for complex structural constraints.
motivation: Improve correctness and structural integrity of LLM-generated hardware designs to enable practical synthesis.
method: Multi-stage reasoning-enhanced training framework: (1) compilation filtering dataset curation achieving 100% pass rate, (2) function-aligned differentiated revision for comparative annotation across five RTL-relevant dimensions, (3) supervised fine-tuning using reasoning prompts, (4) reinforcement learning guided by Verilator parser for functional validation.
key_novelty: Function-aligned differentiated revision methodology annotating RTL code across five dimensions, combined with reasoning-enhanced training.
contributions: Compilation filtering achieving 100% pass rate on curated hardware generation dataset
Function-aligned differentiated revision for multi-dimensional RTL annotation
Reasoning-enhanced training with Verilator-guided RL improving pass@1 by up to 20%

metrics.accuracy: 20% improvement in pass@1 on VerilogEval Human benchmarks

baselines: existing hardware generation LLMs (27-44% pass rate)
limitations: Approach requires Verilator; limited to Verilog/RTL generation without full system-level verification.
